title: River Raisin, 1813: Kentucky’s winter defeat in Michigan
summary: Kentucky volunteers who mustered at Georgetown in 1812 were defeated at the River Raisin in January 1813 by British troops and Wyandot-led warriors.

items.text: Kentucky volunteers rendezvoused at Georgetown Aug 15 1812 (marker 508).
About 800 warriors, Wyandot, Shawnee, Potawatomi, Odawa, Ojibwe; Wyandot chiefs Roundhead and Walk-in-the-Water; resisting American expansion since Greenville.
Jan 18 Frenchtown taken; Jan 22 Procter's attack, Winchester captured, ~500 surrender; ~359 killed, 495 captured/missing (Grokipedia); British 24 killed; Native losses unrecorded.
30-60 wounded prisoners killed; 'massacre' framing American; causes debated (revenge, Procter's failure to guard).
Remember the Raisin, Thames; nine counties named (marker 508); Ballard captured, Simpson killed.

sources.citation: National Park Service: River Raisin National Battlefield Park

openQuestions: Casualty totals vary by source (Grokipedia also gives 'over 400' killed in another section); marker says not half of 1,050 reached home.
Number killed Jan 23: 30–60 per Grokipedia; other accounts higher.
